rationale: Records the executed drift-bound probe (experiment 23d38c5cec9a43a89539bf38b3623b09-experiment, receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4, all nine generated tests passed) and answers the parent investigation's registered gap 838461385f784f74af057837ff488a66-gap-3 from it. The receipt shows the drift is neither bounded nor repaired: eight further re-synchronization rounds took both followers from accepted 6 / decided 6 to accepted 14 / decided 14 one index per round while the leader kept its own accepted index at 6 and its decided index followed to 14 with an unreadable decided log in every round; a leader change onto one of the inflated followers did not reset the accounting (that node kept accepted 14 instead of re-deriving its six indices of content), the previously truthful replica was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7, and in the three following rounds the followers' accepted indexes reached 18 and 10 while the decided index froze at 14 because no write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covered the further reports. No guarded drain, sample or leader change panicked over the eleven rounds. This update therefore (a) revises the parent question-level interpretation into a five-class account, (b) revises knowledge e65d63f4057d4c5bbe8390ac06b30fce-knowledge-2, which claimed the reported decided index follows the drift, into the narrower claim that it follows only while a write quorum covers it and that a leader change re-inflates the truthful replica instead of repairing the accounting, and (c) answers gap-3 as resolved. It also rewrites the parent discriminator to the next open direction and launches the probe for it: the over-compaction case stopsign_overcompaction_then_resync compacts the new leader inside its drifted decided index so that the compacted index moves past the reported accepted index of a live replica, then re-synchronizes that replica (with a replica above the compacted index as a control), so that the decisive observation - a panic or a silently empty suffix on the below-compacted re-synchronization - becomes an executed result rather than a source reading. No other records are changed: the two child accounts (trim, snapshot) and their gaps stand, and the new receipt is cited only for the parent account.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the over-compaction case stopsign_overcompaction_then_resync: three re-synchronization rounds, a leader change onto one of the inflated followers, a local snapshot on that leader inside its drifted decided index, and then the re-synchronization of the replica whose reported accepted index is below the resulting compacted index, with a replica whose index is at or above it as a control. Every drain and every sample is panic-guarded. Previously generated cases are unchanged.

scope.description: Ten cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network; the new case drives the drift, changes the leader, compacts the new leader past a live replica's reported accepted index and then lets that replica re-synchronize, reporting any panic as an event field rather than aborting the run.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot; ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } with default ServerConfig (batch_size 1); BLE messages are dropped, as in the lineage.

Three rounds of node1.reconnected(3) plus node2.reconnected(3) reproduce the drifted state (followers accepted 9, leader decided 9 over six indices of content); node1.try_become_leader() then makes node 1 the leader and re-synchronizes the other two, which in the lineage left node 3 at accepted 7 against the drifted decided index.

The snapshot is requested with the leader's own decided index as the bound and local_only = true, so no Compaction message is sent to the peers and the compacted index becomes that decided index (the StopSign is no longer counted as decided in the drifted state, so the bound is not lowered).

reconnected(pid) is called with the current leader, because the library only starts a re-synchronization when the peer named is the leader; every drain and sample runs inside catch_unwind, so a panic inside a handler becomes an event field instead of aborting the run.
excluded: No entry type with use_snapshots() true is used in the new case, so the snapshot branch of create_log_sync is not exercised there.
No load, timer, message loss or node restart is exercised; only reconnected() calls and one leader change.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

parameters.compaction_bound: the new leader's own decided index at the time of the call

experiment.prefix: Same prefix as the lineage: node 3 leads, five entries are appended and decided, then a StopSign is proposed with reconfigure() and decided, so every node holds six indices of content and reports accepted 6 / decided 6 (OVER_BASE). The new case then performs three rounds of node1.reconnected(3)+node2.reconnected(3), each drained and sampled per node as OVER_R{k}_N{pid} for k = 1..3, reads the leader's decided index, elects node 1 with try_become_leader() and samples as OVER_AFTER_CHANGE, calls node1.snapshot(Some(decided), true) and emits OVER_SNAP with the outcome, the panicked flag, the compacted index, the accepted index and the decided index of the leader, then calls node3.reconnected(1) (the replica whose reported accepted index is below the compacted index) with a guarded drain and samples, emits OVER_LAG_RESULT with the panicked flag, repeats the same for node2.reconnected(1) as the control and emits OVER_AHEAD_RESULT, and finally emits OVER_RUN_END with the number of messages delivered. Every sample records accepted_idx, decided_idx, decided_eq_accepted, is_reconfigured, the read of index 5, the read of index 6, the read of the decided suffix from 0 and its length.
semantic_changes: Adds the over-compaction case stopsign_overcompaction_then_resync and the resync_guarded helper; every previously generated case is unchanged apart from sharing one execution.

comparisons.description: The snapshot call that compacts the leader inside its drifted decided index completes on its own without panicking.

The re-synchronization of the replica whose reported accepted index lies below the compacted index is handled without a panic: no handler may be brought down by a prefix request below the compacted index.

Control: the replica whose reported accepted index is at or above the compacted index re-synchronizes without a panic, so any panic in the other stage is not attributable to re-synchronization as such.

investigations.discriminator: Whether a compaction whose bound comes from the drifted decided index moves the compacted index past a live replica's reported accepted index, so that the next re-synchronization of that replica asks the leader for a prefix below the compacted index. The decisive observation would be a panic or a silently empty suffix on that request rather than a consistent re-sync. The re-synchronization drift itself is no longer the open question: it was shown to continue one index per round over eight rounds, to be unrepairable by a leader change, and not to panic (receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4).

knowledge.statement: Repeated re-synchronizations of replicas that already hold the StopSign make the cluster's reported accepted index drift one further index per round while the log content stays fixed, and while the drifting reporters hold a write quorum the leader keeps adopting the maximum reported accepted index as its decided index: over eight further rounds both followers went from accepted 6 / decided 6 to accepted 14 / decided 14 while the leader's own accepted index stayed 6, its decided index followed to 14 and its decided-log read returned nothing in every round. The drift neither saturates nor is repaired inside the sealed configuration: a leader change onto one of the inflated followers left that node at accepted 14 instead of re-deriving its six indices of content, the previously truthful replica was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7, and in the three following rounds the followers' accepted indexes rose to 18 and 10 while the decided index froze at 14 because no write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covered the further reports.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster after a decided StopSign, each round being a pair of public reconnected() calls addressing the current leader, with nothing else proposed. Observed over three rounds in receipt 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d (followers 7 then 8 then 9 at events 41, 42, 44, 45, 47, 48; leader decided 7 then 8 then 9 with accepted 6 at events 43, 46, 49) and over eight rounds plus a leader change plus three further rounds in receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 (baseline accepted 6 / decided 6 events 9-11; followers accepted 7 at events 12, 13 and 14 at events 33, 34; leader accepted 6 with decided 7 and 14 and an unreadable decided log at events 14, 20, 35; after the leader change node 1 at accepted 14 / decided 14, node 2 at accepted 15, node 3 at accepted 7, events 36-38; last round node 2 at accepted 18 and node 3 at accepted 10 with decided 14, events 46, 47; eleven guarded stages with zero panics, event 48). The decided index stopped following once the reports outran every write quorum; no bound on rounds or on the reported values was reached, and the run stopped after eleven rounds by construction.
knowledge.changed_premise: Narrows the claim that the reported decided index always follows the drift. It follows only while the drifting reporters reach a write quorum in the same term: with the new leader's own recorded indexes lagging, the decided index stopped at the drifted value of 14 while the followers' accepted indexes continued to 18 and 10, so the newest drift shows up as accepted indexes that no longer reach a decision. The revision also records that a leader change re-inflates the previously truthful replica instead of repairing the accounting, and that eleven rounds with eleven guarded stages produced no panic.

interpretations.rationale: One index-space error in the StopSign accounting, five witnessed classes of consequence in nine receipts of one lineage, and the drift is neither bounded nor repaired inside the sealed configuration. Cause: sync_log adds the StopSign carried by a LogSync on top of sync_idx plus the suffix length while the sender's resume point may already count that StopSign, and create_log_sync never shifts sync_idx for a StopSign the sender already holds. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and is given a resume point that covers it ends one index past its content: follower after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), follower re-promising in an ordinary new term with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), the leader that takes over from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), and two followers under a snapshot-capable entry type (fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51, 52). Each such replica stops reporting its reconfiguration as decided and its decided-log read loses the entries (one element or nothing against six before). (2) The index drifts one step per re-synchronization round rather than settling: three consecutive reconnection rounds took the followers from 7 to 8 to 9 over unchanged content and the leader's decided index followed (6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 41-49). (3) A write quorum of drifted reports makes the leader decide the reported index although it holds fewer entries (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24; snapshot-capable: fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 event 53), after which the leader no longer reports the reconfiguration as decided and its decided log is unreadable. This decision needs two drifted reporters in a three-node cluster: with one, the leader stayed consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9). (4) Both compaction paths inherit the drifted values and act on them: trim(None) took the minimum recorded accepted index, which had drifted above the leader's content, and compacted index 7 for a log of six indices, with the region then reported trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15); snapshot(Some(8), false) was accepted inside the drifted decided index, advanced the compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries the log contained, so the entries are no longer reachable and the snapshot that represents them is empty (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). Both calls returned success on input the documentation allows. (5) The drift neither saturates nor is repaired, and it does not crash the replicas (2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4). From the healthy baseline of accepted 6 / decided 6 with a readable six-element decided log on all three nodes (events 9-11), eight further rounds of the same two-follower re-synchronization took both followers to accepted 14 / decided 14, one index per round with no saturation (events 12, 13, 18, 19, 33, 34), while the leader's own accepted index stayed 6 and its decided index followed to 14 with its decided-log read returning nothing in every round, from the first round on (events 14, 20, 35). A leader change was then performed onto node 1, one of the inflated followers: it took the lead in a new term and still reported accepted 14 and decided 14 instead of re-deriving its six indices of content (event 36), node 2 reported accepted 15 against decided 14 and node 3 -- the previously truthful leader, which held six indices -- was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7 (events 37, 38), so the drift spread to the replica that had stayed honest rather than being repaired. The three following rounds left the new leader at accepted 14 / decided 14 and took node 2 to accepted 16, 17, 18 and node 3 to accepted 8, 9, 10 while the decided index stayed at 14 (events 39-47): once no write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covers the further reports the decided index stops following, so the later drift appears as accepted indexes that never reach a decision, and the leader's decided index remains thirteen indices above the content it holds and its decided-log read remains unusable (node 2 read an empty decided log at events 45, 46, 47). No guarded drain, sample or leader change panicked over the eleven rounds (event 48: rounds 11, panics 0, 154 messages delivered). Comparisons 0-4 of that receipt are violated with witnesses 33, 34, 35 and 36 (the fifth additionally records nodes 2 and 3 as outside its applicability); comparisons 5-7 came out unknown because their declared admissions put a node condition on the prerequisite and a node-less identity on the panic event, so those states are asserted from the sampled events named above rather than from comparison outcomes. Controls: the pre-change samples and the no-reconnect control kept six indices of content, a six-element decided log, the StopSign at its own index and the reconfiguration reported as decided (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11, 19-21; 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 38-40; fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 48-50; 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 9-11).

838461385f784f74af057837ff488a66-gap-3.explanation: Resolved by the drift-bound receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4: nothing inside the sealed configuration bounds or repairs the drift within the tested range. Eight further re-synchronization rounds kept adding exactly one index per round to both followers (accepted 7 at events 12, 13 up to accepted 14 at events 33, 34) while the content stayed at six indices and the leader's decided index followed to 14 with an unreadable decided log in every round (events 14, 20, 35). The leader change is not a repair: the new leader, itself re-synchronized earlier, kept its inflated accepted index of 14 rather than re-deriving six (event 36), and the replica that had remained truthful until then was re-synchronized to accepted 7 (event 38). The drift then continued as accepted indexes only: node 2 reached 16, 17, 18 and node 3 reached 8, 9, 10 while the decided index froze at 14 (events 39-47), so the bound on the decided index in this pattern is quorum arithmetic rather than an explicit limit, and no counter, storage guard or automatic repair was observed at any stage. Eleven guarded stages with 154 delivered messages produced zero panics (event 48), so the unrepaired drift is silent: every call succeeded and no endpoint reported an error.

knowledge.assertion: sync_log adds the carried StopSign on top of sync_idx plus the suffix, and each further re-synchronization adds another index
the decided-log read loses the entries after such a re-synchronization
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log
a candidate leader syncing from a follower is inflated in its own accepted index

the reported accepted index drifts one index per re-synchronization round, the decided index follows only while a write quorum covers it, and a leader change re-inflates the truthful replica instead of repairing the accounting
trim accepted a drifted bound and compacted past the content the leader held
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11; 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 9-11), and in the newterm case the new leader and the node that received nothing stayed consistent (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 events 9, 10), so the deviation follows a re-synchronization whose resume point covers the StopSign.

The leader-side decision at a drifted index requires a write quorum of drifted reporters in one term (two of three nodes); one drifted reporter left the leader consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9), and in the drift-bound receipt the decided index stopped advancing once the reports outran every write quorum (2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 46, 47 against decided 14).

The compaction consequences need the drift to cover every node the bound is derived from: trim's bound is the minimum recorded value, so a truthful replica would keep it honest (76cabb0efc3b4eda8eda8c9c79025550-interpretation-0), and the snapshot witness used a request strictly inside the drifted decided index because the StopSign equal case lowers the bound.

The documented reconfiguration flow expects a new instance once a node observes StopSign(ss, true), narrowing the window in which a user reads the old instance; the drift still hides that observation from the leader and, once compaction acts, removes the entries themselves.

The drift cannot be turned into new client values through the append path: append() refuses with PendingReconfigEntry while a StopSign is stored, which is the case throughout every observed drifted state, so the consequence set stays with index accounting, readability and compaction rather than with mis-assigned entries.
limitations: The drift was exercised for eleven rounds with one mid-run leader change; that range found no bound and no repair, but the decided index stopped following once the reports outran every write quorum, so how far the decided index can keep following is a quorum property that was observed with one three-node pattern rather than characterised in general.
Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised; the producers observed are explicit reconnected() calls and an ordinary leader change onto a node that had already drifted.

Only three-node clusters were used, with in-memory storage, no persistence across restarts and one snapshot-capable entry type; the compaction witnesses depend on that entry type's snapshot semantics.

Several comparisons in the repeated-rounds, trim, snapshot and drift-bound receipts came out unknown because their admissions shared event names across cases in one execution or put a node condition on the prerequisite; those states are asserted from the sampled operands, with the violated comparisons cited above.

The drift-bound case samples after each drained round, so it does not show intermediate states inside a round, and it does not exercise the forwarded compaction messages that a snapshot or trim call would send to peers.

The consequence set stays within index accounting, readability and compaction; the sealed configuration admits no further entries and refuses appends while the StopSign is stored, so no value is mis-assigned.
interpretations.joint_history: Nine receipts of one harness lineage, each read on its own samples and never combined arithmetically: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 (resync, control), 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 (single resync, read of index 6), 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 (newterm), dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea (staleleader), fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 (snapshot-capable resync), 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d (three reconnection rounds), ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a (drift then trim), e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c (drift then snapshot) and 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 (drift-bound probe: eight further rounds, a leader change onto an inflated follower, three further rounds). Each successor reproduces the earlier witnesses and adds one case; the drift-bound receipt runs in the same file and the same execution discipline as the others, with the earlier cases unchanged.
